mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 9.0% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 9.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3 years is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based contraction in consumer demand, which typically triggers a sell-off in equities; the joint decline over the past month predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline from the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3 years is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below 100), the manufacturing sector contraction signals reduced corporate output and potential earnings cuts, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over 3 years is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation rate (CPIAUCSL annual change below 1.5%) indicates weak demand and potential deflationary pressures, which typically lead to lower real interest rates and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL annual inflation is below 1.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 100,000 monthly additions signals weak job growth, which typically leads to reduced consumer confidence and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS < 100000, or the Rank IC over 3 years is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a dual shock to the supply side and labor market, which typically triggers a sharp equity sell-off; the joint occurrence predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines and UNRATE rises from prior month, or the Rank IC over 3 years is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high consumer spending (RSAFS above 350,000 million dollars), the strong retail sector signals robust economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 350000, or the Rank IC over 3 years is less than 0.03.
